recommendation:
BOTTOM LINE
Build one deterministic text front-end (pure Python, CPU, about 2-6 s cold start and about 7 ms per line warm on M5/py3.12) that turns raw lyrics into an immutable Song -> Line -> Word -> Syllable(display unit) -> AlignUnit(phonetic unit) tree. Every node carries a [start,end) char span into a canonical display string. Every AlignUnit carries `reading` (sung form in native script) and `roman` (aligner tokens restricted to [a-z'], the exact MMS_FA vocabulary). The aligner gets a flat list of AlignUnit romans and the times come back by index. Each mapping is an index lookup, so nothing has to be recovered by string matching. I implemented and tested the prototype on Python 3.12.15 / macOS arm64: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sunjaewon-projects-Performance-live-lyrics-tracking/a1551f14-1847-4d65-a2d8-137d02c33533/scratchpad/research/syllables/scripts/lyricsprep.py (454 lines). Sample inputs/outputs are in .../syllables/data/mixed.txt(.json) and edge.txt(.json). All span round-trip asserts pass.

RECOMMENDED STACK (Python 3.12; 3.11 also fine. Do NOT use 3.13+ because python-mecab-ko, needed by g2pk2, ships arm64 wheels only for cp38-cp312)
- Japanese readings: pyopenjtalk-plus 0.4.1.post9 (MIT; arm64 wheels cp310-cp314; imports as `pyopenjtalk`). It clearly gave the best lyric readings in my comparison. On 明日->アシタ, 何を->ナニヲ, 走り出せ->ハシリダセ, 2人->フタリ, 1000年->センネン and 3月14日->サンガツジューヨッカ it was the only engine that got all of them right. unidic-lite, sudachi and pykakasi each failed several: アス, ナン, ハシリデセ, 2ニン, イチレイレイレイネン, and pykakasi read 今日の日 as にち. `run_frontend()` gives per-word `string`/`read`/`pron`/`mora_size`. Use `read` (orthographic kana) for okurigana alignment and mora display, and `pron` (ー long vowels, は->ワ, を->オ) for romanization. Strip the accent mark ’ from `pron`.
- Japanese romaji for display (optional "romaji line" for the singer): cutlet 0.5.2 (MIT, 2026-07) + fugashi 1.5.2 + unidic-lite 1.0.8. Set `use_foreign_spelling=False`, otherwise you get "Tokyo tower", "love song". Do not use cutlet for alignment tokens. Use the mora table instead, because it gives a per-mora 1:1 mapping.
- Korean: 1 hangul block = 1 display unit = 1 align unit. Romanize with uroman 1.3.1.1 (the romanizer MMS was trained with; MIT-style license plus an attribution clause). Romanizing each syllable separately gives the same result as romanizing the whole string; I verified this for hangul. Optional pronunciation-aware layer is g2pk2 0.0.3 (Apache-2.0) + python-mecab-ko 1.3.7 (BSD). Call it per word, and accept its output only if it is still pure hangul of the same length, otherwise fall back to orthographic. For pure hangul it preserves the block count (꽃잎을 -> 꼰니블). It mangles numbers and English (24시간->이사시간, 2명->이명, R&B->아&비, baby->베이비), so never feed it digits or Latin.
- English: hybrid syllabifier. Target count comes from CMUdict (`cmudict` 1.1.3; take the min count over its pronunciations). If the word is not in CMUdict, count vowel groups with a silent-e rule. Split points come from pyphen 0.18.1 `Pyphen(lang='en_US')` with the DEFAULT left/right margins. Then reconcile: merge the shortest neighbouring pieces while there are too many, and split the piece with the most effective vowel groups while there are too few. Results: Ev|ery morn|ing, beau|ti|ful, to|night (pyphen alone: tonight), some|bo|dy (pyphen alone: some|body), ly|rics, re|mem|ber, e|mo|tion, B|T|S. Romans for MMS are just the lowercase orthographic letters of each piece, so pieces concatenate exactly back to the word.
- Numbers: Japanese numbers go to pyopenjtalk, which handles counters. Korean uses a native-counter rule (살/명/개/시/번째/시간/마리/잔/번...) with native forms (한/두/세/네/스물한...), else num2words(lang='ko') Sino-Korean, and appends 퍼센트 for %. English uses num2words 0.5.14 (LGPL). Every number becomes ONE display unit that holds N align units (e.g. "21" -> 스.물.한) and is flagged needs_review=True so the operator confirms the sung form in the prep UI.
- Script detection: the `regex` package (2026.9.29) with \p{Hangul} \p{Hiragana} \p{Katakana} \p{Han} \p{Latin}. Pitfall: ー, 〜 and ・ are Script=Common, so add them explicitly or use \p{scx=Katakana}.

JAPANESE DISPLAY RULES (implemented)
- Mora segmentation: a small ゃゅょぁぃぅぇぉゎ attaches to the preceding single kana. っ, ー and ん are each their own mora. Tested: ティ|ー|ン, ヴァ|イ|オ|リ|ン, デュ|エ|ッ|ト, ちょ|っ|と.
- Kana surfaces get one display unit per mora.
- Kanji runs are split from okurigana with a regex built from the surface (kanji run -> (.+?), kana -> literal), matched against the reading: 走り出せ -> 走[はし]|り|出[だ]|せ, 食べ物 -> 食[た]|べ|物[もの]. Each kanji run becomes ONE display unit holding its morae (東京 -> と.う.きょ.う). The UI renders <ruby> and wipes across the unit using the per-mora times. This is the standard karaoke convention, so there is no need to split jukujikun per kanji.
- User furigana overrides the analyzer: {漢字|かんじ}, ｜漢字《かんじ》, 漢字(かんじ), 漢字（かんじ）, 漢字[かんじ]. A '.' inside the reading ({東京|とう.きょう}) requests a per-kanji split. The parenthesis form only counts as furigana when the content is kana and it immediately follows Han characters, which keeps it distinct from backing vocals like (oh oh).
- Romanization uses my own Hepburn-ish table restricted to [a-z]. It is mora-exact, unlike uroman's EDGES output, which merges っ into the next mora (2-4 'tto') and ー into the previous one ('raa'). Context is resolved per LINE, across word boundaries: っ becomes the next consonant (ch -> t, e.g. 待|っ|て -> ma-t-te), ー/〜 becomes the previous vowel, and a final っ with nothing usable gets roman "" (it inherits time). 〜/~ in Japanese is treated as ー for analysis. An orphan 〜 after a unit extends that unit (空〜 -> so.ra.ー).

DOES KOREAN PRONUNCIATION (연음/비음화) MATTER FOR CTC ALIGNMENT?
Partly. This is my reasoning; I have not measured it on audio yet.
(1) Pure liaison (잎을 -> 이플) gives the same CHARACTER sequence (ip+eul vs i+peul = 'ipeul'), so a char-level CTC path is identical. Only the attribution of the consonant to a display syllable changes. That decides whether a syllable's start time lands on the note onset (pronunciation form) or about one consonant-duration (~30-120 ms) late (orthographic form). For a karaoke wipe the pronunciation form is better.
(2) Assimilation rules change the letters themselves (ggoc -> ggon, ip -> nip, tensification g -> gg). That makes the transcript closer to what is acoustically sung, but g2pk2 bugs (꼰니블 instead of 꼰니플, cross-word 날려 -> 랄려 when called on whole lines) introduce wrong letters.
Recommendation: generate both variants (orth and pron), align both with MMS_FA, keep the one with the higher mean per-frame log-prob. That costs one extra emission pass, or none, since the emission can be reused and only the Viterbi rerun. Call g2pk2 per word, not per line. The same argument favours Japanese `pron` (tookyoo) over `read` (toukyou) as the romaji source.

SPECIAL TOKENS AND NORMALIZATION POLICY
- Ingest: NFC, then per-char NFKC EXCEPT the Hangul compatibility jamo block U+3130-318F (NFKC turns ㅋㅋ into conjoining ᄏᄏ). Then curly quotes -> straight, drop zero-width chars, collapse spaces. The NORMALIZED text is the canonical display text, so NFKC length changes (ｶﾞ 2->1, ㌔ 1->2) never break spans.
- Blank line(s) increment the stanza counter.
- Section headers: a line that is only [Chorus], 【サビ】, Chorus:, 후렴 etc. sets Line.section. If a header is followed by no lyric lines (or text like 후렴 반복 / ※くり返し / Repeat Chorus), expand it into a copy of the previous section with that label in the performance sequence.
- Repeat marks at line end: x2, ×2, (x3), *2, (2번), (2回). Line.repeat=N. Expand N line instances in the SUNG ORDER sequence that the aligner and tracker use. The display may show one line with a badge or N lines. Store timings per instance, not per Line.
- Whole-line (…) or （…） sets Line.backing. Inline (hold me) sets Word.kind='backing'. Both are excluded from the main alignment transcript by default; insert MMS's '*' star token there to absorb them. Render them dimmed. In vocal-only live mode the lead singer may not sing them at all.
- Symbols: & -> and / 앤 / アンド; % -> percent / 퍼센트 / パーセント; acronyms (R&B, BTS, AT&T) are spelled as letter names, one display unit per letter. Laughter jamo (ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ) is not sung: no align units. Punctuation and spaces are never display units; the UI renders uncovered characters with the state of the preceding syllable.
- English words inside Korean/Japanese lines always go through the English path (script-run split), never through g2pk2 or OpenJTalk transliteration.
- Elongations (yeahhh, Ooooh): CMUdict lookup after collapsing 3+ repeated letters. Display is kept verbatim.

DATA MODEL
Use a static text tree plus separate timing arrays.
- Song { id, default_lang, lines[], sections[], sequence[] (sung order: {instance_id, line_idx, rep_k}) }
- Line { idx, text (canonical display), raw, lang, stanza, section, backing, repeat, words[] }
- Word { text, span, lang (ko|ja|en|x), kind (lex|num|sym|backing), reading, needs_review, syllables[] }
- Syllable (display unit) { text, span, units[] }
- AlignUnit { reading, roman, (t0, t1 per instance) }
Stable ids like L12.W3.S1.U0. align_tokens() flattens to [(li,wi,si,ui,roman)] skipping empty romans, in the same order as the MMS transcript list. Syllable time = (first unit t0, last unit t1). The tracker builds a sorted array of syllable start times per instance and binary-searches the reference time to get (syllable id, intra-unit progress) for the WebSocket push.

alternatives.name: pykakasi 2.3.0 (ja kanji->kana/romaji)
alternatives.pros: Pure Python, fast load (0.06 s), simple API, handles some lyric readings (明日->あした).
alternatives.cons: GPL-3.0-or-later. Dictionary-only, no morphological context: 今日の日->きょうのにち, 2人->2にん. Does not convert particles (は->ha). Readings are noticeably worse than pyopenjtalk-plus. Repo moved to Codeberg (GitHub mirror still active).

alternatives.name: fugashi 1.5.2 + unidic-lite 1.0.8 (or unidic 1.1.0 full) for ja readings
alternatives.pros: MIT/BSD (UniDic is GPL/LGPL/BSD tri-licensed, choose BSD). Exact surface tokens, so char spans are trivial. Gives both kana and pron fields. Needed anyway by cutlet. Wheels cp39-cp314.
alternatives.cons: unidic-lite is UniDic 2.1.2 from 2013 (248 MB installed). Reads 明日 as アス, 何を as ナン, 走り出せ as ハシリデセ, and digits get no reading (2人->2ニン). Full unidic needs `python -m unidic download` (~1 GB on disk).

alternatives.name: sudachipy 0.7.0 + sudachidict-core 20260723.1
alternatives.pros: Apache-2.0, actively maintained (2026-09), cp310-abi3 arm64 wheels, good normalization and split modes A/B/C. Already pulled in by pyopenjtalk-plus.
alternatives.cons: reading_form() only (no pron, so no long-vowel/particle phonetics). 1000年->イチレイレイレイネン, 走り出せ->デセ. Dictionary.create() is deprecated in favour of Dictionary.tokenizer().

alternatives.name: uroman EDGES for Japanese kana instead of a custom mora table
alternatives.pros: Same romanizer as MMS training. RomFormat.EDGES returns (start,end,txt) char spans, which are reversible.
alternatives.cons: Edges merge っ into the following mora ([2-4] 'tto') and ー into the preceding one ([0-2] 'raa'), so they are not mora-aligned. Kanji are romanized as Chinese pinyin (東京->dongjing), so kana conversion has to happen first anyway.

alternatives.name: korean-romanizer 0.28.0 / hangul-romanize 0.1.0 (Korean RR)
alternatives.pros: Revised Romanization that humans can read (korean-romanizer applies some sound rules: kkochipeul). Good for a display romanization line.
alternatives.cons: korean-romanizer is GPL-3.0. hangul-romanize is stale (2020) with no license declared. Neither matches what MMS_FA was trained on (uroman), so use them only for display.

alternatives.name: g2pk (0.9.4, 2020) / g2pkk 0.1.2 / g2pk3 1.4 instead of g2pk2
alternatives.pros: Same Kyubyong g2pK rule set. g2pkk targets Windows (eunjeon). g2pk3 (MIT) adds a Japanese transliteration and a fix for rule 20.
alternatives.cons: g2pk needs konlpy + Java. All are forks of an unmaintained 2020 codebase with the same number/English bugs, and none fixes alignment-relevant issues. g2pk2 is the least-friction option on macOS py3.12.

alternatives.name: Phoneme-level path (g2p_en 2.1.0 / pyopenjtalk.g2p / jamo) for a phoneme CTC or MFA aligner
alternatives.pros: Better if the aligner is phoneme-based (wav2vec2 espeak phoneme models, MFA korean_mfa / japanese_mfa).
alternatives.cons: g2p_en 2.1.0 (2019) breaks with nltk>=3.9 unless you nltk.download('averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng'). It garbles K-pop and acronyms (BTS->B IY1 T S) and drops '&'. pyopenjtalk.g2p loses mora boundaries, so derive phones per mora from the mora table instead. Not needed for MMS_FA, which is character-level.

alternatives.name: syllables 1.1.5 / pysyllables 1.0.3 for English
alternatives.cons: Counts only, no split positions. syllables is GPL-3.0. pysyllables is unmaintained since 2019. CMUdict + vowel-group fallback already covers this.

key_facts.claim: uroman Python API: Uroman().romanize_string(s, lcode=None, rom_format=RomFormat.STR|EDGES|ALTS|LATTICE). EDGES returns Edge objects with .start/.end/.txt/.type. Korean edges are exactly one per hangul block. Japanese edges merge っ with the next mora and ー with the previous one. Kanji are romanized as Mandarin pinyin (東京->dongjing).

torchaudio 2.11.0 (2026-03-23) still exports functional.forced_align, merge_tokens and pipelines.MMS_FA / Wav2Vec2FABundle, even though the 2.8/2.9 docs say these APIs 'will be removed in 2.9'. The MMS_FA labels are '-' (blank) + a i e n o u t s r m k l d g h y b p w c v j z f ' q x + '*' (star). The tokenizer takes List[str] (one entry per 'word') and the aligner returns List[List[TokenSpan]] per entry.

key_facts.claim: The MMS_FA tutorial's normalize_uroman applies lowercase, ’->', any char not in [a-z' ] -> space, then collapses spaces. Digits are silently deleted, so numbers must be verbalized beforehand. The model was trained on 23k hours in 1100+ languages, and the tutorial says CJK requires segmentation first.

g2pk2 keeps the hangul block count for pure-hangul input (꽃잎을->꼰니블, 같이->가치, 좋아해->조아해, 읽고->일꼬). It is wrong on numbers (24시간->이사시간, 2명의->이명의, 10년->심년), converts English to hangul (baby->베이비, R&B->아&비), and has rule errors (꼰니블 should be 꼰니플). Each call takes about 15 ms.

g2pk2 side effects: its module import calls nltk.download('cmudict') (it wrote ~/nltk_data/corpora/cmudict during my test at 14:54), and G2p() runs `pip install python-mecab-ko` via subprocess if the `mecab` module is missing.
g2p_en 2.1.0 fails on nltk 3.10.3 with LookupError for 'averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng'. It works after nltk.download('averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng').
key_facts.source: Local test with NLTK_DATA in scratch

key_facts.claim: pyphen en_US with left=1,right=1 produces garbage (o-h-o-h, rhyth-m, I'l-l, y-ou're). Default margins are fine but under-split (tonight, gonna, lyrics, Tokyo unsplit; somebody->some-body). Reconciling to the CMUdict count fixes most of these.

NFKC changes length for half-width dakuten kana (ｶﾞ: 2->1) and squared words (㌔: 1->2), and converts Hangul compatibility jamo (ㅋ U+314B) into conjoining jamo (U+110F). ー (U+30FC), 〜 (U+301C) and ・ are Script=Common, so they do not match \p{Katakana}.

Prototype runtime on M5 Pro / py3.12: about 1.8-6 s cold start (OpenJTalk dictionary about 2 s, g2pk2+mecab about 1.5 s, cmudict 0.15 s), then about 0.41 s for 63 mixed lines (about 6.5 ms/line), giving 770 align tokens. Installed disk: pyopenjtalk 125 MB + sudachidict_core 193 MB + mecab_ko_dic 112 MB (+ unidic_lite 248 MB if cutlet is used).

For char-level CTC, Korean liaison (연음) leaves the character sequence unchanged and only moves syllable boundaries toward note onsets. Assimilation changes letters, so its benefit depends on g2p accuracy. Pick the orth or pron variant per song by the CTC score.
key_facts.source: Reasoning from MMS_FA char-level design; not yet measured on audio

# Full tested module: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sunjaewon-projects-Performance-live-lyrics-tracking/a1551f14-1847-4d65-a2d8-137d02c33533/scratchpad/research/syllables/scripts/lyricsprep.py
# Install (Python 3.12 venv):
#   uv pip install "pyopenjtalk-plus==0.4.1.post9" "uroman==1.3.1.1" "g2pk2==0.0.3" "python-mecab-ko==1.3.7" \
#       "pyphen==0.18.1" "cmudict==1.1.3" "num2words==0.5.14" "regex==2026.9.29"
#   optional display romaji: "cutlet==0.5.2" "fugashi==1.5.2" "unidic-lite==1.0.8"
#   export NLTK_DATA=<project>/.nltk_data   # g2pk2 downloads cmudict at import time

# ---------------- data model (static text tree; timings filled per sung instance) ----------------
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
@dataclass
class AlignUnit:  reading: str; roman: str; t0: float|None=None; t1: float|None=None   # ko syllable / ja mora / en syllable
@dataclass
class Syllable:   text: str; span: tuple[int,int]; units: list[AlignUnit]                 # DISPLAY unit (東京 = 1 unit, 4 morae)
@dataclass
class Word:       text: str; span: tuple[int,int]; lang: str; kind: str="lex"; reading: str=""; syllables: list[Syllable]=field(default_factory=list); needs_review: bool=False
@dataclass
class Line:       idx: int; text: str; raw: str; stanza: int; section: str|None=None; backing: bool=False; repeat: int=1; words: list[Word]=field(default_factory=list)
# Song.align_tokens() -> [(li, wi, si, ui, roman)] skipping roman=="" ; Song.sequence = sung-order line instances (repeat/section expansion)

# ---------------- ingest normalization (spans index into THIS string) ----------------
import unicodedata, regex as re
_QUOTES = str.maketrans({"’":"'","‘":"'","“":'"',"”":'"'})
def normalize_lyrics(text):
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text).translate(_QUOTES)
    out = "".join(c if 0x3130 <= ord(c) <= 0x318F else unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", c) for c in text)  # keep ㅋㅋ
    return "\n".join(re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", l).strip() for l in unicodedata.normalize("NFC", out).splitlines())

# markup: repeat marks, ruby, sections, backing
REPEAT_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|\s)(?:\(\s*)?[x×✕*]\s*(\d+)\s*\)?\s*$|\s*\(\s*(\d+)\s*(?:x|×|번|回)\s*\)\s*$", re.I)
KANA = r"\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}ー・."
RUBY_RE = re.compile(rf"\{{(?P<b1>[^|{{}}]+)\|(?P<r1>[{KANA}]+)\}}|[|｜](?P<b2>[^《]+)《(?P<r2>[{KANA}]+)》"
                     rf"|(?P<b3>[\p{{Han}}々〆ヶ]+)[(\[（](?P<r3>[{KANA}]+)[)\]）]")
SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[\[【]\s*([^\]】]+?)\s*[\]】]\s*$|^\s*(verse|chorus|hook|bridge|pre-?chorus|outro|intro|rap|후렴|サビ)\s*\d*\s*:?\s*$", re.I)
BACKING_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[(（](.+)[)）]\s*$")
TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"(?P<acr>[A-Z](?:[&][A-Z])+)|(?P<en>\p{Latin}+(?:'\p{Latin}+)*)|(?P<num>[0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)*%?)"
                      r"|(?P<ko>\p{Hangul}+)|(?P<ja>[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Han}ー々〆ヶ〜]+)|(?P<sp>\s+)|(?P<sym>[&+@#%])|(?P<punct>.)")
# strip_markup('明日(あした)また x2') -> ('明日また', [(0,2,'あした')], 2)

# ---------------- Korean ----------------
import uroman as ur
U = ur.Uroman()
def mms_clean(s): return re.sub(r"[^a-z']", "", unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", s.lower()))
def ko_syllables(word, start, g2p=None):          # g2p = g2pk2.G2p() or None
    pron = word
    if g2p and re.fullmatch(r"\p{Hangul}+", word):
        p = g2p(word)                               # call PER WORD; never with digits/Latin
        if len(p) == len(word) and re.fullmatch(r"\p{Hangul}+", p): pron = p
    return [Syllable(c, (start+i, start+i+1), [AlignUnit(pc, mms_clean(U.romanize_string(pc)))])
            for i, (c, pc) in enumerate(zip(word, pron))]
# 꽃잎을 -> 꽃|잎|을 roman ggon-ni-beul (pron) / ggoc-ip-eul (orth)
def ko_jamo(ch):                                    # no-dependency decomposition
    n = ord(ch) - 0xAC00

NATIVE_COUNTERS = ("살","명","개","시","번째","마리","잔","번","사람","시간","달","가지")
NATIVE = {1:"한",2:"두",3:"세",4:"네",5:"다섯",6:"여섯",7:"일곱",8:"여덟",9:"아홉",10:"열",20:"스물",30:"서른",40:"마흔",50:"쉰",60:"예순",70:"일흔",80:"여든",90:"아흔"}
def ko_number(n, next_text):
    if 0 < n < 100 and next_text.startswith(NATIVE_COUNTERS):
        t, o = n//10*10, n%10; return (NATIVE.get(t,"") if t else "") + (NATIVE[o] if o else "")
    from num2words import num2words; return num2words(n, lang="ko")      # 24시간 -> 스물네, 100 -> 백

# ---------------- Japanese ----------------
import pyopenjtalk   # from pyopenjtalk-plus
SMALL = set("ぁぃぅぇぉゃゅょゎァィゥェォャュョヮ")
def morae(kana):
    out = []
    for ch in kana:
        if ch in SMALL and out and len(out[-1]) == 1 and out[-1] not in "っッーんン": out[-1] += ch
        else: out.append(ch)
    return out
_B = dict(zip("あいうえおかきくけこがぎぐげごさしすせそざじずぜぞたちつてとだぢづでどなにぬねのはひふへほばびぶべぼぱぴぷぺぽまみむめもやゆよらりるれろわゐゑをんゔぁぃぅぇぉゃゅょゎ",
  ("a i u e o ka ki ku ke ko ga gi gu ge go sa shi su se so za ji zu ze zo ta chi tsu te to da ji zu de do na ni nu ne no "
   "ha hi fu he ho ba bi bu be bo pa pi pu pe po ma mi mu me mo ya yu yo ra ri ru re ro wa i e o n vu a i u e o ya yu yo wa").split()))
def k2h(s): return "".join(chr(ord(c)-0x60) if "ァ" <= c <= "ヶ" else c for c in s)
def mora_roman(m):
    m = k2h(m)
    if m in ("っ","ー","〜"): return "?"            # resolved per line
    b = _B.get(m[0], "")
    if len(m) == 1: return b
    s = _B.get(m[1], "")
    if m[1] in "ゃゅょ": return (b[:-1] if b in ("shi","chi","ji") else b[:-1]+"y") + s[-1]
    return {"u":"w","i":"y","ku":"kw","gu":"gw"}.get(b, b[:-1]) + s   # ティ ti, ファ fa, ウィ wi, ヴァ va
def resolve_context(units):                          # run over ALL units of a line (crosses words)
    r = [u.roman for u in units]
    for i, x in enumerate(r):
        if x != "?": continue
        if units[i].reading in ("っ","ッ"):
            nxt = next((y for y in r[i+1:] if y and y != "?"), "")
            r[i] = "t" if nxt.startswith("ch") else (nxt[0] if nxt and nxt[0] not in "aiueo" else "")
        else:
            prv = next((y for y in reversed(r[:i]) if y and y != "?"), "")
            r[i] = prv[-1] if prv and prv[-1] in "aiueo" else ""
    for u, x in zip(units, r): u.roman = x
HAN = re.compile(r"[\p{Han}々〆ヶ]")
def okurigana_split(surface, reading_hira):         # 走り出せ/はしりだせ -> [(走,はし),(り,り),(出,だ),(せ,せ)]
    parts = re.findall(r"[\p{Han}々〆ヶ]+|[^\p{Han}々〆ヶ]+", surface)
    m = re.fullmatch("".join("(.+?)" if HAN.match(p) else f"({re.escape(k2h(p))})" for p in parts), reading_hira)
    return list(zip(parts, m.groups())) if m else None
def ja_nodes(text):                                  # re-anchor OpenJTalk nodes to input spans (2人 -> 二人)
    nodes = [(n["string"], n["read"], n["pron"].replace("’","")) for n in pyopenjtalk.run_frontend(text)]
    norm = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text); out, pos, pend = [], 0, []
    for s, rd, pr in nodes:
        ns = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s); j = norm.find(ns, pos) if ns.strip() else -1
        if j == pos or (j > pos and pend):
            if pend: out.append(((pend[0][0], j), "".join(p[1] for p in pend), "".join(p[2] for p in pend))); pend = []
            out.append(((j, j+len(ns)), rd, pr)); pos = j+len(ns)
        elif re.fullmatch(r"[\p{P}\p{S}\s]*", ns): continue
        else: pend.append((pos, rd, pr))
    if pend: out.append(((pend[0][0], len(norm)), "".join(p[1] for p in pend), "".join(p[2] for p in pend)))
    return out   # [((s0,s1), read_kata, pron_kata)]
# per node: rm=morae(k2h(read)); pm=morae(k2h(pron)) (fallback rm if counts differ); roms=[mora_roman(m) for m in pm]
# kanji chunk / number -> Syllable(chunk, span, [AlignUnit(rm[k], roms[k]) ...n morae]); kana chunk -> 1 Syllable per mora
# replace 〜/~ by ー before run_frontend (same length) so wave-dash lengthening gets a mora.

# ---------------- English ----------------
import pyphen, cmudict
CMU, HY = cmudict.dict(), pyphen.Pyphen(lang="en_US")       # default margins! left=1/right=1 is broken
VG = re.compile(r"[aeiouy]+", re.I)
def n_vg(c): n = len(VG.findall(c)); return n-1 if n > 1 and re.search(r"[^aeiouy]e$", c, re.I) else n
def en_count(w):
    w = w.lower(); prons = CMU.get(w) or CMU.get(re.sub(r"(.)\1{2,}", r"\1\1", w))
    if prons: return min(sum(p[-1].isdigit() for p in pr) for pr in prons)
    return max(1, n_vg(w))
def en_syllables(word, start):
    n = en_count(word); parts = HY.inserted(word, hyphen="\x00").split("\x00")
    while len(parts) > n:
        i = min(range(len(parts)-1), key=lambda j: len(parts[j])+len(parts[j+1])); parts[i:i+2] = [parts[i]+parts[i+1]]
    while len(parts) < n:
        i = max(range(len(parts)), key=lambda j: n_vg(parts[j])); g = list(VG.finditer(parts[i]))
        if len(g) < 2: break
        cut = g[0].end() + max(0, g[1].start()-g[0].end()-1); parts[i:i+1] = [parts[i][:cut], parts[i][cut:]]
    out, p = [], start
    for part in parts: out.append(Syllable(part, (p, p+len(part)), [AlignUnit(part, mms_clean(part))])); p += len(part)
    return out    # Every morning -> Ev|ery morn|ing ; somebody -> some|bo|dy ; tonight -> to|night

# ---------------- feeding MMS_FA and mapping back (API names verified in torchaudio v2.11.0 source) ----------------
import torch, torchaudio
bundle = torchaudio.pipelines.MMS_FA
model = bundle.get_model(with_star=True)            # dict incl. '*' star token for backing/ad-libs
tokenizer, aligner = bundle.get_tokenizer(), bundle.get_aligner()
units = song.align_tokens()                         # [(li,wi,si,ui,roman)]
transcript = [r for *_, r in units]                 # one MMS "word" per AlignUnit (may insert "*" between lines)
with torch.inference_mode():
    emission, _ = model(wave16k)                    # (1, T, 29)
spans = aligner(emission[0], tokenizer(transcript)) # List[List[TokenSpan]] aligned 1:1 with units
sec = wave16k.size(1) / emission.size(1) / bundle.sample_rate
for (li, wi, si, ui, _), sp in zip(units, spans):
    u = song.lines[li].words[wi].syllables[si].units[ui]
    u.t0, u.t1 = sp[0].start * sec, sp[-1].end * sec
# Syllable time = (units[0].t0, units[-1].t1); units with roman=="" inherit neighbour times.
pitfalls: Python version: python-mecab-ko 1.3.7 (needed by g2pk2) has macOS arm64 wheels only for cp38-cp312. misaki also requires <3.13. Pin the venv to 3.12 (or 3.11). mecab-ko 1.0.2 has cp313 wheels, but g2pk2 imports the module `mecab` from python-mecab-ko.

g2pk2 import side effects: nltk.download('cmudict') into the first writable nltk path (it created ~/nltk_data/corpora/cmudict on this machine during my test; harmless, ~1.7 MB, remove it if unwanted), and G2p() runs `pip install python-mecab-ko` via subprocess if it is missing. Set NLTK_DATA to a project dir and preinstall the deps.

g2pk2 is wrong on numbers and English (24시간->이사시간, 2명->이명, R&B->아&비, baby->베이비) and makes rule errors (꽃잎을->꼰니블). Called on a whole line it applies cross-word liquidization (날려->랄려). Call it per hangul-only word and require same length plus pure hangul; otherwise use orthographic.

uroman romanizes kanji as Mandarin pinyin (東京->dongjing): always convert Japanese to kana first. uroman EDGES are not mora-aligned for っ and ー, and uroman leaves digits untouched. The MMS normalizer then deletes them, so a verse silently loses words unless numbers are verbalized first.

pyopenjtalk run_frontend() rewrites the surface (2人->二人, ASCII->full-width, symbols dropped). Never assume node strings concatenate to the input. Re-anchor with NFKC + find and group the unmatched gap (implemented in ja_nodes). The `pron` field contains accent marks ’ that must be stripped. The first call takes about 2 s (dictionary load).

Use OpenJTalk `read` (orthographic kana) for okurigana matching and mora display, and `pron` for romanization. They have the same mora count in practice, but guard it (fallback to read when counts differ), and guard kana chunks whose surface mora count differs from the reading (make them one unit).

The okurigana regex is non-greedy and can mis-split rare words. When fullmatch fails, fall back to one display unit for the whole word; never drop morae (zip truncation silently loses units, which is why the mora-count guard exists).

cutlet's default use_foreign_spelling=True outputs English spellings for katakana loanwords (タワー->tower, ラブソング->love song) and has a built-in exception list (Tokyo). Use it only for a human romaji line, never for alignment tokens.
unidic-lite reads digits as nothing (2人->2ニン) and has a 2013 vocabulary. sudachi reads 1000 digit by digit (イチレイレイレイ). Both misread 走り出せ as ハシリデセ. Do not use them as the reading source.
pyphen with left=1,right=1 produces nonsense splits (o-h-o-h, rhyth-m, I'l-l). Keep the default margins. Words containing hyphens or apostrophes must be split or tokenized before hyphenation.
g2p_en 2.1.0 is broken on nltk>=3.9 (needs 'averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng'), and it mishandles acronyms (BTS) and '&'. Avoid it for the MMS path, since English needs only letters there.

Unicode: ー (U+30FC), 〜 and ・ are Script=Common, so \p{Katakana} misses them. NFKC changes string length (ｶﾞ 2->1, ㌔ 1->2) and turns ㅋ/ㅠ compatibility jamo into conjoining jamo. Normalize once at ingest (per-char NFKC excluding U+3130-318F) and make that string the canonical display text.

Repeat marks and section re-references change the SUNG ORDER. The aligner transcript and tracker timeline must use the expanded sequence, otherwise the second chorus is aligned against nothing. Store timings per line instance, not per text line.

Backing vocals in parentheses: Demucs-style vocal stems usually contain them, but a live lead-vocal mic may not. Exclude them from the main transcript (use the MMS '*' star token as a sink) and do not let the tracker wait on them.

Romanized units must never be empty when passed to the MMS tokenizer. Skip roman=='' units (e.g. a final っ) and give them interpolated times. CTC needs at least one frame per token plus blanks between repeated letters; very dense fast rap may need the star token or line-level fallback.

The torchaudio docs banner says forced_align/MMS_FA would be 'removed in 2.9', but the v2.11.0 source still exports them. Pin torchaudio and re-check on every upgrade (GitHub issue pytorch/audio#3902).
open_questions: Which aligner will the alignment track pick (MMS_FA char CTC vs a phoneme CTC / MFA vs Whisper-based word timestamps)? The roman field targets MMS_FA. A phoneme aligner needs a per-mora/per-syllable phone field, and a Whisper-based one would use the char spans of the original text instead.

Korean orth vs pron romanization: does the pronunciation-aware variant actually improve syllable-onset accuracy on separated K-pop vocals? This needs a small labelled test (e.g. 3 songs, onset error in ms). The proposed per-song CTC-score selection is untested.
Should English display units be per syllable (Ev|ery) or per word with a syllable-timed wipe? The second looks cleaner on a teleprompter. The data model supports both.

Operator review UX for needs_review items (numbers, symbols, acronyms, ambiguous Han-only lines between ja/zh/ko-hanja): confirm in the prep UI before alignment, or auto-accept and fix after a test run?
Are furigana or romaji overlays wanted on the prompter (for non-native singers)? If so, add cutlet (ja) and korean-romanizer (GPL) or a custom RR for display only.

Licensing intent: if the app will be distributed closed-source, swap the GPL pieces (cmudict PyPI wrapper -> raw BSD cmudict.dict file; avoid pykakasi and korean-romanizer; use pyphen under LGPL/MPL). Also keep the uroman acknowledgement sentence required by its license.
